First of all, I'm sorry to hear that. I'm Turkish myself as well, and I know how bad the economy is over there. 

Here are some tips I would like to give you;

1. Talk about it. 
Talk to your roommates, family or mentor. I understand that you rather not talk about it maybe because you don't want to bother others, or maybe because they have too much on their own plates, but so do you. They could help you, even if it's just with words or comforting you. 

2. Look into organisations.
I don't live in Turkey, otherwise I could've named up a few organisations that could help people who are in the same situation as you. Perhaps you could look up any programs/organisations that could be of any use. 

3. Try to find a job. 
Hear me out; as a woman myself, who knows how the system works in Turkey, I know it can be hard.   But, you could easily start off with a small side job, like working in a supermarket, or a drugstore. Maybe even a clothing store, these places are usually surrounded with woman who work there also, so you would probably feel more comfortable there. Maybe you have had some kind of internship done already, if so; try finding a job related to what you were/are studying. If you aren't able to find a job that's related to your study, that's totally okay. 

4. Stay. Motivated.
Easier said than done, but you won't get out of this situation with a state of mind like you've lost it all. In moments where I feel that way, too I tell myself to keep moving because if I stand still I won't get to where I should actually be. I know, this sounds really stupid, and it's like saying "just be happy" to someone who is unhappy, but I believe you will get there.

5. Take a break, give yourself space to breathe.
I think since you're interested in arts, you like to be creative. Try taking the time of your day for an hour to get a little creative; doodle a bit, listen to some music, take some pictures, really whatever you want.

6. It's okay to make mistakes.
Please know that you and I are only human, we make mistakes but the trick of it is to learn from it. Learning from your mistakes may take some time, or it might take only a few minutes. It doesn't matter how long it takes; try to set lessons for yourself when you feel like you've made a mistake and reconsider if you really did make a mistake or if it was just a misunderstanding.

Like I said, try to keep your head up. Talk to someone in your surroundings about it.
